chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim and Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): In

the man says to his wife, 'Make my concubine permissible for me, for I dislike that you see me exposed,' so she makes her permissible for him. He (peace be upon him) said, 'It is not permissible for him from her except that (exposure), and he does not have the right to touch her or have intercourse with her.' Hisham added: 'Does he have the right to visit her?' He said, 'It is not permissible for him except what she said.' And that which indicates that whenever her private part becomes permissible to him, whatever else becomes permissible to him is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the scope of permission when a master's wife makes his concubine permissible for him upon his request?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the scope of *Istirja'* (re-marriage) for a master regarding his slave concubine, establishing that the wife's declaration of permission is strictly limited to the specific act mentioned—here, visual exposure—rather than granting full sexual rights. Shia jurists utilize this distinction to demonstrate that marital permissions are not automatically comprehensive but are bound by the explicit intent (*niyyah*) and wording of the granting party, a principle derived from the Prophet’s confirmation that 'he is not permitted anything other than what she said.'
